Thanks Bethany — good and concise.

Summary of what Redwood can commit (high level):
- Version pinning: we can pin a cluster to a specific runtime+model bundle for a maintenance window. Pinning is explicit and reversible; it prevents automatic rollouts and autoscaler-triggered model swaps.
- Rollback path: two options
  1) Fast rollback: unpin + trigger previous image rollout (expect 6–12 minutes per node depending on image size; plan for staged canary then fleet).
  2) Evacuation: redirect traffic to a fallback Dedicated or hosted variant (if configured) while nodes are remediated — typically used if the change impacts startup or disk-level upgrades.
- Post-patch telemetry: per-node health, token latency P50/P95, error-rate diff, and a KV-coldness metric (to detect cache invalidation regressions). We will post a short telemetry bundle to the shared Drive link.

Requested from ACME:
- Confirm an 8-hour maintenance window target (we recommend 0100–0900 UTC to minimize traffic).
- Confirm whether you have a fallback Hosted/Dedicated endpoint we can route to in case of evacuation.
- Point us to the change ticket/Jira so we can attach our runbook and evidence.

Attaching a draft Pin Matrix (spreadsheet) and a concise evacuation runbook for your SOC review.

I'll loop Karthik for technical pin/rollback details and Monica for scheduling & comms.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Bethany / ACME ops — adding technical detail on pin semantics and safe rollback sequencing: 

Pin semantics (short):
- Pin = immutable mapping in the cluster manifest: (runtime_sha, model_bundle_tag). Nodes will reject auto-updates while pinned.
- Pins are per-cluster and can be time-bounded (we can set expiry to auto-unpin).

Rollback / evacuation sequencing (recommended):
1) Canary: apply patch to 2–3 canary nodes isolated from warm pools. Observe KV cache hit-rate & latency for 30–45 minutes.
2) Gradual rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with 15–30 minute observation windows.
3) If P50 latency increase > 20% or errors spike > 0.5% absolute, abort rollout: immediately stop further rollouts and restore previous image on canaries.
4) Fast unpin & fleet revert: unpin operation triggers controller to reconcile previous tag; we estimate 10–25 minutes for full revert on an average 20-node cluster (network-bound).
5) Evacuation to fallback: if node-level rollback not possible (disk changes, taints), we will flip routing at the ingress layer to the pre-provisioned fallback endpoint — this requires a short DNS/route change and smoke tests (~5–12 minutes).

Caveats & asks from ACME:
- Please provide VPN access window and a service account for runbook automation (we also support offline signed approvals if the environment is air-gapped).
- If you want automatic pin expiry, we need to agree on a conservative expiry (we suggest 72 hours).

Logistics: we'll keep a hotline (Zoom + Slack channel) during the window. I can prepare the exact CLI commands for unpin/unroll and the controller audit logs that will be captured.

-Karthik
